## Summary

Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron main process: init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap, graceful degradation when Steam is absent, and a minimal preload context-bridge API so the renderer never touches the SDK directly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `electron/main.ts` initialises Steamworks (with `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary` + app ID bootstrap, e.g. `steam_appid.txt`) and logs a clear warning when Steam is unavailable.
- [ ] The launcher boots and is fully functional without Steam (dev / non-Steam runs) — no crash, web app unaffected (intake AC5).
- [ ] `electron/preload.ts` exposes a minimal `steamFollow` API via contextBridge: `isSteamAvailable`, `openStorePage(appId)`, `isFollowing(devAccountId)`, `claim(...)` (as confirmed by F1).
- [ ] Renderer code has zero direct Steam SDK imports (enforced by F2's interface contract).
- [ ] `npm run build` succeeds with the Steamworks native module packaging config (Windows primary target per launcher item).
- [ ] All F2 unit tests still pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Steamworks init module behind the `FollowSource` interface (F2).
- Preload context bridge exposing `steamFollow`.
- electron-builder config updated for the native module (Windows primary).

## Dependencies

- F2 (interface contract).
- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (launcher provides electron/main.ts, electron/preload.ts structure).

## Deliverables

- `electron/main.ts` Steamworks init, `electron/preload.ts` bridge, packaging config.
data.title: F3: Steamworks SDK integration in launcher

## Summary

Game-agnostic unlock logic: a config-driven catalog of three bundled games; the player picks exactly one free unlock when the follow is confirmed, and the choice persists across launches.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Follow confirmed (per F1 mechanism) triggers the unlock flow offering a choice of exactly one of three configured games; the other two remain locked (reserved for future milestones).
- [ ] Unlock persists across launches — a player who followed once keeps the game with no re-verification prompt on every boot (intake AC3).
- [ ] Game-agnostic: the bonus list is config-driven (e.g. `electron/bonus-catalog.json`), no specific game title is hard-coded (intake AC4).
- [ ] Launcher's game list reflects lock/unlock state: unlocked game playable; others shown locked with milestone messaging.
- [ ] Steam unavailable → unlock state queryable but inactive; web app fully functional (intake AC5).
- [ ] All F2 unit tests pass (mocked follow source + persistence).

## Minimal Implementation

- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new): follow check via `FollowSource`, catalog resolution, local persistence (unlock flag + chosen game).
- Wire the choose-one-of-three UI (launcher game list / modal).
- No Steam-specific logic in the renderer beyond the `steamFollow` bridge API.

## Dependencies

- F1 (mechanism decision), F2 (tests), F3 (Steamworks init + bridge).

## Deliverables

- `electron/steam-follow.ts`, `electron/bonus-catalog.json`, unlock UI, unit tests.
data.title: F4: Unlock logic — choose-one-of-three bonus

## Summary

Add an SLL-compliant "Follow us on Steam" CTA to the tutorial's final (completion) step. In the launcher it opens the Steam store page via Steamworks overlay / steam:// URL and re-checks the follow on return; in browser mode it still shows the CTA but only opens the Steam page (no reward).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The tutorial's last step (T16 in Main Street's unified tutorial flow) shows the "Follow us on Steam" CTA using SLL-compliant layout (no hardcoded pixels).
- [ ] Launcher mode: clicking opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client (player already logged in — no browser login prompt) via `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` or `steam://store/<appid>` (intake AC1).
- [ ] On return to the launcher, the follow is re-checked (per F1 mechanism) and the F4 unlock flow triggers on confirmation.
- [ ] Browser/web mode: CTA still renders; clicking opens the Steam store page (steam:// URL if Steam client present, else web store page); copy reflects that no reward is granted in the browser; app remains fully functional (intake AC5).
- [ ] CTA interaction provides visual/audio feedback per the audio/visual-feedback requirement and respects reduced-motion.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the tutorial's final step definition + localized copy (i18n) with the CTA.
- Store-page open handler in main process; browser-fallback URL logic.
- Follow re-check on window focus/overlay close in launcher mode.

## Dependencies

- F3 (preload bridge), F4 (unlock flow). Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.

## Deliverables

- Tutorial T16 CTA (SLL layout + i18n), store-page open handler, browser fallback, browser test.

## Goal

Make "won a game" a first-class, engine-generic achievement event so the give-away triggers have a real, Steam-free source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AchievementSystem` (or a documented thin extension) gains an idempotent game-outcome surface (e.g. `onGameOutcome({ gameId, outcome })`) that unlocks mapped achievements via the existing `AchievementSink`; zero Steam/Electron imports.
- The launcher manifest defines `first-win` and `second-distinct-game-win` meta-achievements (titles, descriptions, hidden flags) and the outcome-to-achievement mapping is engine-generic.
- "Second distinct game" logic only unlocks after wins in two different game ids; re-wins of the same game do not.
- `SteamAchievementService` idempotence and offline paths are reused unchanged for the meta-achievements.
- Unit tests cover outcome-to-unlock, distinct-game counting, idempotence, and no-op for unknown outcomes; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `electron/achievement-manifest.json`
- `tests/steam-achievements/achievement-outcome.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Engine outcome surface, manifest meta-achievements, unit tests.

## Goal

A main-process service that evaluates the give-away config against locally-unlocked achievements and persists game unlocks through the shared store, reachable from the renderer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GiveawayService` reads `SteamAchievementService.getUnlocked()`, evaluates the F1 contract against the give-away config, and persists unlocks to the unified `ContentUnlockStore`; it runs on launch and after each achievement unlock and never throws.
- `SteamFollowService` and `GiveawayService` share one unlock store so the Game Selector has a single source of truth; existing follow unlock behaviour is preserved and its existing tests still pass.
- IPC channels plus `electron/preload.cjs` expose give-away status/progress and a refresh call; channel names stay in sync and every handler is total.
- With Steam, the manifest, or the config absent the service degrades to a safe no-op (no fabricated unlock, no crash) and the web build is unaffected.
- Unit tests (mocked sources/stores) cover launch evaluation, post-unlock evaluation, idempotence, cross-launch persistence, and missing-dependency degradation; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`
- `electron/steam-achievements-ipc.ts`
- `electron/steam-follow-ipc.ts`
- `electron/preload.cjs`
- `electron/main.ts`
- `tests/steam-giveaways/giveaway-service.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Give-away service, unified store wiring, IPC/preload surface, unit tests.

# Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend

External producer action (Steamworks partner backend). Depends on the Steamworks
project/App ID existing. The launcher manifest
(`core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`) declares the in-game achievement API
names; the Steamworks backend must declare the exact same names or Steam
silently drops the unlock.

## Goal / user story

As the Tableau Card Engine producer, I need every Main Street achievement
registered on Steam with the exact API name from the launcher manifest, so that
in-game unlocks appear for players.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All 13 Main Street achievements declared in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` are registered in the Steamworks backend with API names matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>` exactly.
2. `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` is registered with the secret/hidden flag OFF, consistent with the manifest's `hidden: false`.
3. End-to-end evidence: a packaged launcher run against the local Steam client completes a mapped challenge and the achievement unlocks on the Steam profile.

## Constraints

- Producer/external action — not implementable by a code agent.
- API names must match the manifest byte-for-byte.
- Blocks **MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7** (Serial Seller manifest entry / Steamworks API name).

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ**: Challenges as achievements (epic)
- **CG-0MUNC7EAM004E6GN**: F5: Real Steamworks achievement adapter
- **MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7**: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name (blocking consumer)
data.title: Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend

data.description:
# Intake Brief — Cutting a release from a game uses the TCE version number

**Work item:** CG-0MVGF2QE9008NA5R — Cutting a release from a game uses the TCE version number

## Problem statement

When a release is cut from a game repo such as `tce-main-street`, the game ends up versioned with the Tableau-Card-Engine (core) version number. Each game repo must maintain its **own** independent version, decoupled from the core's release cadence.

## Users / user stories

- **Game maintainers (agents + operators)** cutting a release of a sibling game repo:
  "As a maintainer of `tce-main-street`, I want the game's release version to reflect the
  game's own release history, so players can tell the game version apart from the engine version."
- **Players and testers** reading the version label on the game selector / game screens:
  "As a playtester, I want the version I report in feedback to identify the game build
  (and be meaningful on its own), not silently mirror the engine version."
- **Engine maintainers** composing the multi-repo distribution:
  "As an engine maintainer, I want a game's release version to be independent of the
  engine's, so engine releases and game releases can proceed at different cadences."

## Root-cause analysis (evidence)

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson()` writes the game repo's
  `package.json` with `version: manifest.version ?? '0.0.0'`, where `manifest` is the
  **core's** `package.json` (`readCoreManifest(coreRoot)`). A new or re-scaffolded game
  therefore inherits the core's current version number.
- The behaviour is pinned by a test: `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
  asserts `expect(pkg.version).toBe('9.9.9')` (the stubbed core manifest version).
- Observed in the wild: every `tce-*` sibling carries a core-derived version —
  0.1.17 for the batch scaffolded 2026-09-26 (the core version at that date), and
  0.1.21 for `main-street` / `the-rising`, whose releases tracked the core's version
  patch-for-patch (core v0.1.17→v0.1.21, main-street v0.1.17→v0.1.21).
- **Not the cause:** the ship skill's `bump-version.js` resolves the **invoking repo's**
  root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and bumps that `package.json`, so once a
  game repo carries its own version its releases bump correctly. The coupling is
  seeded at scaffold time and then persists.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No core-version coupling in the scaffold.** `renderPackageJson()` no longer derives
   the game's version from the core manifest: a freshly scaffolded game repo's
   `package.json` `version` is the independent baseline `0.1.0` (producer decision), and
   a re-scaffold of an existing game repo **preserves** the version already in that
   repo's `package.json` rather than overwriting it.
2. **Existing game repos are not renumbered.** The work does not rewrite sibling game
   repo versions: `golf` / `blackjack` / `coloretto` / `feudalism` / `lost-cities` /
   `sushi-go` / `beleaguered-castle` (0.1.17), `the-rising` (0.1.21) and `main-street`
   (0.1.21) keep their current numbers and diverge naturally on their next release.
   A re-scaffold of any of them is version-neutral (verified for at least one repo, or
   covered by the unit-test preserve case).
3. **Scope limited to the scaffold seeding path, with the ship path verified.** Only the
   scaffold seeding + its tests/docs change; a verification note records that the ship
   `bump-version.js` reads the invoking repo's own `package.json` (no shared/release-code
   change required). Any newly discovered version-leak path is filed as a follow-up work
   item rather than folded into this one.
4. **Tests.** Unit tests cover: (a) a new-game scaffold seeds `0.1.0`; (b) a re-scaffold
   of an existing repo preserves its version; (c) no test asserts core-version coupling
   (the `'9.9.9'` assertion is replaced). Tests must exercise real `package.json`
   read/write behaviour, not merely assert rendered strings in isolation.
5. **Documentation.** The per-game version policy is documented (each game owns its
   version; the scaffold seeds `0.1.0` and preserves on re-scaffold; a game release bumps
   only that game's version) in the new-game guide and/or the multi-repo architecture
   scaffold section.
6. **Quality gates.** `npm test -- --project unit` and `npm run build` pass with the
   change; all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not edit the global ship skill or any `skill/` tree (`AGENTS.md` repository
  boundary); the bump logic is already repo-local and needs verification only.
- Push to `dev` only. Cross-repo game changes (if any) are recorded on this core work
  item or in the game repo's own Worklog store.
- `renderPackageJson` stays a pure render function: the preserve-on-re-scaffold decision
  must be injected/explicit (e.g. an existing-version parameter or a read in
  `scaffoldGameRepo`), keeping the template unit-testable.
- Do not add a hard-coded per-game version table — the policy is generic.

## Existing state

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` is the single generator for every `tce-<game>` repo
  `package.json`; it is invoked via `npm run scaffold:game` / `scaffold:games` (core),
  `npm run scaffold` (game repos) and `scripts/setup-distribution.ts`.
- `ScaffoldOptions` carries `coreManifest?: CoreManifest`; `CoreManifest.version` is
  typed optional and only used for the game version stamp.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` has a `renderPackageJson` describe block
  and a `scaffoldGameRepo` integration block using a temp sibling layout.
- Game repos carry `__APP_VERSION__` injected from **their own** `package.json` in their
  `vite.config.ts` (generated by the same scaffold), so display follows the package
  version automatically once seeding is fixed.
- `configs/engine-pin.json` in each game repo records the engine **commit** (not a
  version), so engine/game version independence has no other data coupling.

## Desired change

- Seed a new game repo at `0.1.0`; preserve an existing repo's version on re-scaffold.
- Keep `renderPackageJson` pure and explicit about the version it writes.
- Replace the core-version-coupling test with baseline + preserve coverage.
- Document the per-game version policy (who owns a game's version, how a release bumps
  it, and why it is not the engine version).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson()` (drop `manifest.version`; take an explicit version), `ScaffoldOptions`, `scaffoldGameRepo()` (read the existing `package.json` version before writing).
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — replace `expect(pkg.version).toBe('9.9.9')` with baseline + preserve cases; add a re-scaffold integration case against a temp repo with an existing version.
- `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` — §3 scaffold stage: state the seeded baseline and that games own their version.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 "Per-game repo scaffold": version-ownership note alongside the existing `package.json` description.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Build-Time Version Injection: clarify the label shows the **composing repo's** version (game repo ⇒ game version, core ⇒ engine version).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — re-scaffold clobbers a released version.** If the preserve path reads the
  wrong file or a stale path, a re-scaffold could reset a game to `0.1.0` and break
  tag↔version correlation. *Mitigation:* preserve is read-then-write inside
  `scaffoldGameRepo` with an integration test on a temp repo that has an existing
  version; unreadable/missing `package.json` falls back to the `0.1.0` baseline.
- **Risk — tests only assert rendered strings** (the existing test's weakness) so the
  real write path stays unguarded. *Mitigation:* AC4 requires integration-level
  coverage of the write path.
- **Risk — scope creep into release tooling.** "Fix the version" invites touching the
  ship skill, CI, or renumbering every game. *Mitigation:* Q3 decision constrains scope
  to the scaffold seeding path; any additional leak found is a follow-up work item.
- **Assumption — `0.1.0` baseline is acceptable before any release exists** (producer
  decision Q1); the first release from a new game therefore tags `v0.1.1` after the
  ship patch bump. Documented rather than special-cased.
- **Assumption — leaving existing versions in place is safe** (producer decision Q2):
  released `main-street` tags `v0.1.18`–`v0.1.21` stay valid; games diverge from the
  engine's numbering at their next release.
- **Assumption — no other core-version coupling exists** (producer decision Q3): the
  ship bump path reads the invoking repo's `package.json`; verified, not modified.

## Related work

### Automated report (find-related)

- **CG-0MSQBQSCX006R02B** — CLI draft-release script (code + docs) (completed)
- **CG-0MM1OQ5U80HVOPKJ** — Inconsistent move validation patterns across games (completed, tangential)
- **CG-0MSQ6MV7N0085V9R** — Local skill: promote Windows Setup artifact to GitHub release (operator-approved) (completed)
- Repository file matches: `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (generic keyword matches)

### Manually linked context

- **CG-0MR89YKN0000FK5W** — Add game version to menu screen and Main Street settings panel (completed): established the version display surface that makes the coupling visible.
- **CG-0MUI9K4F8009DYJL** — Add an ALPHA banner and version number to all game screens (completed): same display surface.
- **CG-0MRZ35LK80064WIS** / **CG-0MRZ0YNCO003J5CN** — CI-3 release checklist (completed): release-cadence context.
- Source: `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` in `../tce-main-street` (engine pin vs dev sync — the only other engine/game coupling data).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 — Initial version baseline for a brand-new game repo

**Question:** When the scaffold creates a **new** game repo (no prior `package.json`), should the game start at `0.1.0`, `0.0.0`, or another baseline?
**Recommended:** `0.1.0` — matches the existing `0.1.x` convention, gives a sensible first release (`v0.1.1`) without implying engine compatibility.
**Answer (producer):** `0.1.0`. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-21).

### Q2 — Existing game repos: renumber now vs leave in place

**Question:** Should existing sibling game repos (currently core-derived: 0.1.17, or 0.1.21 for `main-street`/`the-rising`) be renumbered as part of this work, or left at their current numbers and decoupled from here?
**Recommended:** leave in place — released tags (`main-street` v0.1.18–v0.1.21) already exist; renumbering would orphan tag/version correlation for little benefit.
**Answer (producer):** "as recommended" — leave in place. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-21).

### Q3 — Scope of the version leak

**Question:** Intake identified the root cause as `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderPackageJson()` stamping the core manifest version into game `package.json` (pinned by `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` asserting `pkg.version === '9.9.9'`). Are other paths in scope — e.g. a release accidentally run from the core checkout, or the distribution/launcher build stamping the core version onto games?
**Recommended:** scaffold seeding + test/doc updates only (the ship `bump-version.js` already reads the invoking repo's own `package.json` via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), with the ship path verified rather than modified.
**Answer (producer):** "as recommended" — scaffold seeding + tests/docs only; verify the ship path. Source: interactive reply (2026-10-21).

> Research note for Q3: inspected `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js`
> (`PKG_PATH = resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'package.json')`, `REPO_ROOT = git rev-parse --show-toplevel`),
> `merge-dev-to-main.sh` (same repo-local bump), `scripts/engine-sync.mjs` (pins a commit SHA in
> `configs/engine-pin.json`, no version), and each game's generated `vite.config.ts`
> (`__APP_VERSION__` from the game's own `package.json`) — no additional version-leak path found.

---

## Plan (created by the plan skill, 2026-10-22)

**Decision: single-item plan — no child work items.** The whole change (code +
tests + docs) is one small end-to-end slice that a single implement session can
deliver; child items would add coordination overhead without isolating any
independently shippable behaviour. Effort Small / risk Medium (effort-and-risk
report on this item). Test-first ordering is preserved within the single slice.

**A. Tests first (red) — `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`**
- `renderPackageJson`: a new game renders `version: '0.1.0'` even when the core
  manifest stub declares `9.9.9` (proves decoupling); an explicit version
  argument is written verbatim. Delete the `expect(pkg.version).toBe('9.9.9')`
  assertion.
- `scaffoldGameRepo` integration over the temp sibling fixture, asserting real
  on-disk read/write: (a) a **new** game repo is seeded with `0.1.0`; (b) a
  re-scaffold of a repo whose `package.json` already says `0.1.17` **preserves**
  `0.1.17`; (c) a missing/unparseable existing `package.json` falls back to
  `0.1.0`.
- Verify red: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
  fails for the expected reasons.

**B. Scaffold seeding (green) — `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`**
- Add `export const GAME_INITIAL_VERSION = '0.1.0';` with a comment stating the
  per-game version policy (each game owns its version; decoupled from the core).
- `renderPackageJson(game, manifest, coreRel, version = GAME_INITIAL_VERSION)`:
  write the explicit `version` verbatim; never read `manifest.version`. Keep the
  render function pure — the version is injected (constraint).
- Add `readExistingPackageVersion(gameRepoRoot): string | undefined` — total:
  returns the string `version` from `<root>/package.json`, `undefined` when the
  file is absent, unreadable, or has no string version.
- `ScaffoldOptions.version?: string` explicit override (wins over preserve),
  resolved as `options.version ?? readExistingPackageVersion(root) ??
  GAME_INITIAL_VERSION`.
- `ScaffoldResult` gains `version: string` + `versionSource` (`'explicit'` |
  `'preserved'` | `'baseline'`) and the CLI prints `version: <v> (<source>)`.
- `CoreManifest.version` stays typed (a package.json subset) but is documented
  as unused by the scaffold, so test stubs can keep declaring it to prove
  decoupling.
- Verify green: targeted unit tests + `npm run build`.

**C. Documentation**
- `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` §3 — seeded baseline `0.1.0`, preserve on
  re-scaffold, games own their version (AC5).
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 — `package.json` bullet: version
  ownership note (AC5).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` Build-Time Version Injection (§) — clarify
  `__APP_VERSION__` shows the **composing repo's** version: game repo ⇒ game
  version, core ⇒ engine version; a game release bumps only that game's version.

**D. Verification note + gates (AC2, AC3, AC6, AC7)**
- Verification note on the work item: the ship `bump-version.js` resolves
  `REPO_ROOT = git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and bumps `PKG_PATH =
  <root>/package.json`; `merge-dev-to-main.sh` does the same; `engine-sync.mjs`
  pins a commit SHA (no version). No shared/release code changed.
- Existing sibling repos are **not** renumbered (verified by reading
  `../tce-*/package.json` — 0.1.17 / 0.1.21 — before and after; no changes).
- Version-neutral re-scaffold of an existing repo is covered by the unit-test
  preserve case (AC2 allows either); a live re-scaffold of a real sibling is
  optional and skipped to avoid churn.
- Gates: `npm test -- --project unit` + `npm run build` pass; full suite
  (`npm test`) run by the test skill before `in_review`.

| 2 existing repos not renumbered; re-scaffold version-neutral | D (verify) + unit preserve case (A) |
| 3 scope limited to scaffold seeding; ship path verified only | D |
| 4 tests (baseline, preserve, no 9.9.9, real read/write) | A |
| 5 per-game version policy documented | C |
| 6 unit tests + build pass; docs updated | D (gates) |
| 7 full suite passes | D (gates) |

### Key Files (updated)
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson()`, new
  `GAME_INITIAL_VERSION` + `readExistingPackageVersion()`, `ScaffoldOptions`,
  `ScaffoldResult`, `scaffoldGameRepo()`, CLI output.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — replace `'9.9.9'` assertion with
  baseline + preserve coverage; add re-scaffold integration cases.
- `docs/dev/creating-a-new-game.md` — §3 scaffold stage.
- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 per-game repo scaffold.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Build-Time Version Injection.

### Assumptions (implementation-level; documented, not blocking)
- Keep the `CoreManifest.version` field typed (subset of package.json) but
  unused by the scaffold.
- Add an optional explicit `version` override to `ScaffoldOptions` / CLI.

Follow-up to [test-failure] @ui barrel statically imports Phaser (CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ) (discovered-from: CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ).

Scope (operator-chosen option C): establish a documented Phaser-free surface for the src/ui modules that downstream node-environment unit tests import. The current fix makes illegalMoveToastView itself Phaser/Renderer-value-free, restoring @ui/shakeIllegalMove and @ui/dragDrop as node-safe entry points. This follow-up records and enforces the convention:

- A documented list (docs/DEVELOPER.md, and a comment block in src/ui/index.ts or a dedicated module) of which src/ui modules are guaranteed node-safe (no Phaser value import at evaluation time) and what is required to keep them that way (type-only Phaser imports, no top-level import of Phaser-bearing modules such as ./Renderer).
- Optionally a static import-graph check that fails when a listed module transitively has a value import of 'phaser' (stronger than the evaluation-based guard; catches regressions without depending on test execution order).
- Clarify in docs that the @ui barrel is intentionally Phaser-bearing (CardGameScene extends Phaser.Scene) and that node tests must import deep Phaser-free paths rather than '@ui' itself.

Non-blocking; small task.
